texts.preamble: Saurabh vs Rajveer Singh on 21 April, 2025 :1: In The Court Of Ms. Charu Gupta Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01 (Se), Saket Courts : New Delhi Mact No:1034/18 Saurabh v. Rajveer & Ors. Cnr No: Dlse0100-9253-2018 1. Saurabh S/o Girdhari Lal R/o H.No.57, Dholagarh, Palwal-121102, Haryana 121102 ..........Petitioner Versus 1. Rajveer Singh S/o Sh. Bhagwan Singh R/o Nagla Turkiya Pani ki tanki ke pas, Makkhanpur, Firozabad, U.P. ............Driver/Respondent no.1 2. Manish Bansal S/o Sh. Bishan Kumar Bansal R/o 35 Hanuman Road, Firozabad, U.P. ............Owner/Respondent no.2 3. Royal Sundaram General Insurance Company Ltd. Unit no.801A, 8th floor, Devika Tower, Nehru Place, New Delhi. ............Insurance company/Respondent no.3 Mact No.1034/18 Saurabh v. Rajveer & Ors. P. No. 1 of 25 ss Digitally signed by Charu Charu Gupta Gupta Date: 2025.04.21 16:06:40 +0530 Date of accident : 03.06.2018 Result of accident : Grievous/permanent disability Date of filing of Petition : 13.11.2018 Date of Decision : 21.04.2025 Award 1.
texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Sh. Saurabh suffered grievous injury. An application u/s 166(1) Motor Vehicle Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/applicant. Brief facts of the case are that on 03.06.2018 at about 8 a.m., petitioner/injured Saurabh was riding a motorcycle bearing no.HR-30K-0264. He along with his friend Lalit were coming towards Village Dholagarh, when a speeding car Honda Amaze bearing vehicle no. UP-83AE-5885 (hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle) suddenly hit the motorcycle of victim. Due to the impact, they fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries. Both the victims were removed to the nearest Government hospital from where they were referred to Delhi Trauma Center. 3. An FIR no.0409/18 was registered u/s 279, 337 of IPC at PS Camp Palwal, Distt-Palwal. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed u/s 279/337/338 of IPC before concerned criminal court while two separate claim petitions were filed before this Tribunal by two separate injured i.e. Saurabh and Lalit. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no. 2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Respondent no.3 is the insurer of MACT NO.1034/18 Saurabh v. Rajveer & Ors. P. No. 2 of 25 ss CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.04.21 Date: 16:06:44 +0530 the offending vehicle. 5. No Written statement or reply filed on behalf of Respondent no.1 & 2 despite opportunity. 6. Respondent no.3/insurance company filed his reply denying the occurrence of the accident and refuting the allegations of rash and negligent driving on the part of respondent no.1/driver. It is stated that as per petition, the FIR has been lodged 8 days after the alleged incident and thus the claim be declined as suspicious. 7. Vide order dated 16.08.2021, following issues were framed. OPP 2. OPP. 3. Relief. 8. In order to prove his claim, petitioner examined his father Sh.Girdhari Lal as eye witness PW-1 and Dr. Puneet Kant as PW-2. 9. Sh. Girdhari Lal filed his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He deposed on the lines of the claim petition and stated that on 03.06.2018 he was standing on Dholagarh Mod, Palwal, Haryana Saurabh vs Rajveer Singh on 21 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177001014/ 2 at about 08:00 a.m. his son Saurabh along with his friend namely Lalit were returning from Dholagarh Village to Camp Palwal, Haryana on motorcycle bearing no.HR-30K-0264 which was being driven by his son with due care at normal speed MACT NO.1034/18 Saurabh v. Rajveer & Ors. P. No. 3 of 25Digitally ss signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.04.21 16:06:49 +0530 on the side of the road. As soon as they reached at Dholagah Mod, Palwal, a speeding car bearing no. UP-83AE-5885 came from Hodal Haryana side in rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle of the petitioner from backside with great force, due to which Saurabh and his friend Lalit fell on the road and received grievous injuries. Due to the accident petitioner sustained 90% permanent disability caused by head injury and has now completely lost his future life. He deposed that petitioner is unmarried and was studying in class 10 th prior to the accident. He is unable to take up further studies. PW-1 deposed that he spent about Rs.2,50,000/- on treatment of the petitioner, who is still under the medical treatment. He further deposed that Saurabh was learning electric work and earning Rs.17000/- per month prior to the accident. PW-1 relied upon his Adhar card as Ex.PW1/1, Adhar card of injured Saurabh as Ex.PW1/2, Educational documents as Ex.PW1/3, treatment records along with certified copy of discharge summary of injured as Ex.PW1/4, original medical bills and conveyance bills as Ex.PW1/5, original disability certificate as Ex.PW1/6, certified copy of Medical Legal Report as Ex.PW1/7, certified copy of FIR as Ex.PW1/8, certified copy of Driving Licence of driver of offending vehicle as E x . P W 1 / 9 . Respondent no.3. Dr. Puneet Kant was examined as PW-2. He deposed that he was summoned witness. He brought the copy of medical board opinion regarding disability assessment of patent Saurabh dated 11.03.2021 as Ex.PW1/6. The same has been issued by MACT NO.1034/18 Saurabh v. Rajveer & Ors. P. No. 4 of 25 ss CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2025.04.21 16:06:54 +0530 Safdarjung Hospital, Medical Board. The medical board opinion which was issued by Dr. Suman K. Badhal, Associate professor, Physical and Mental Rehabilitation Department, Safdarjung Hospital, Dr. Shishir Kumar Chandan, Assistant Professor Neurology, Dr. Puneet Kant, Assistant Professor, Dr. Arun Kumar Pandey, Assistant Professor regarding the permanent disability of 90% relating to head injury. He testified that the impact of 90% disability is variable from patient to patient and there are some possibilities like being in bed ridden stage requiring help for day to day activities. He testified that the possibility of death due to such severe head injury is very likely. The 90% disability would be likely render the patient in paralysis/paresis condition. He was duly cross-examined by respondent no.3/insurance company. No evidence was led on behalf of the respondents. Saurabh vs Rajveer Singh on 21 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177001014/ 3 10. It is argued on behalf of the claimants that the accident was caused by respondent no.1 by driving the offending truck in a rash and negligent manner.
texts.arguments: It is argued that since respondent no. 1 was driving the offending vehicle, which is owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no. 3, respondents are liable to compensate the claimant for the injury sustained and the permanent disability incurred. On the other hand, it has been argued on behalf of the insurance company that there is no eye witness to the accident and the eye witness examined by the petitioner has been planted. It is argued that the petitioner was driving without a valid driving licence and without a helmet and as such is liable to deduction on MACT NO.1034/18 Saurabh v. Rajveer & Ors. P. No. 5 of 25 ss CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2025.04.21 16:06:58 +0530 account of contributory negligence. Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 13. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 15. Further, driver of the offending vehicle has not challenged or denied by evidence, his rashness or negligence in driving of the offending vehicle or committing the accident. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 16. Ld. Counsel for insurance company has placed reliance of the decision of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Rehmani Begum vs. Krishan Pal, SLP No.10293/2019, wherein the Hon'ble Delhi High Court upheld the rejection of a claimed on the ground that the deceased motorcyclist was not having a valid driving licence. Reliance is placed upon Pramod Kumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri Vs. Karmasey Kungvargi Tak and Ors. decided by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in C.A. No.5436 of 1994 decided on 05.08.2002, it is held as under: "...9. Subject to non-requirement of the existence of duty, the question of contributory negligence is to be decided on the same principle on which the question of defendant's negligence is decided. The standard of reasonable man is as relevant in the case of plaintiff's contributory negligence as in the case of defendant's negligence. But the degree of want of care which will constitute contributory negligence, varies with the circumstances and the factual situation of the case. The following observation of the High Court of Australia in Astley v. Austrust Ltd.1 is worthy of quoting: "A finding of contributory negligence turns on a factual investi- gation whether the plaintiff contributed to his or her own loss by failing to take reasonable care of his or her person or property. What is reasonable care depends on the circumstances of the case. In many cases, it may be proper for a plaintiff to rely on the defendant to perform its duty. But there is no abso-lute rule. The duties and responsibilities of the defendant are a variable factor in determining whether contributory negligence exists and, if so , to what degree. In some cases, the nature of the duty owed may exculpate the plaintiff from a claim of con-tributory negligence; in other cases, the nature of the duty may reduce the plaintiffs share of responsibility for the damage suffered; and in yet other cases the nature of the duty may not prevent a finding that the plaintiff failed to take reasonable care for the safety of his or her person or property. Contribu-tory negligence focuses on the conduct of the plaintiff. The duty owed by the defendant, although relevant, is one only of many factors that must be weighed in determining whether the plaintiff has so conducted itself that it failed to take reasonable care for the safety of its person or property." Similarly, in Saleem Ahmad v. Jaipal, MAC. App.113/2020 decided on 29.11.2024 wherein following observation was made on the issue of absence of driving licence with the victim: "...13. while considering this aspect of negligence, it must not be forgotten that it is a compensation case under MV Act which is under consideration and unless there is some independent evidence to show that the injured did not know how to drive the motorcycle or MACT NO.1034/18 Saurabh v. Rajveer & Ors. P. No. 9 of 25 ss CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2025.04.21 16:07:15 +0530 had committed any act which contributed or would be attributable to his lack of skill of driving of motorcycle, mere absence of DL or just holding of a learner's licence cannot be a ground to conclude that the appellant was solely negligent in causing the accident. Saurabh vs Rajveer Singh on 21 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177001014/ 6 14. while injured/appellant may be liable to be prosecuted under the penal provision of MV Act for not having a valid DL but only a learner's licence to drive the motorcycle, but the same does not ipso facto attribute sole or contributory negligence in driving the motorcycle..." In the instant case Insurance company/respondent no. 3 has MACT NO.1034/18 Saurabh v. Rajveer & Ors. P. No. 10 of 25 ss CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2025.04.21 16:07:19 +0530 not raised any statutory defence against respondent no.1 or respondent no.2 and has under the contractual liability arising out of the insurance policy /contract of insurance, respondent no. 3 is liable to indemnify respondent no.2 (owner of the offending vehicle) by compensating the petitioner. 19. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680 . The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) MACT NO.1034/18 Saurabh v. Rajveer & Ors. P. No. 11 of 25 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 20.6. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder: On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government MACT NO.1034/18 Saurabh v. Rajveer & Ors. P. No. 13 of 25 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.04.21 16:07:32 +0530 service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as MACT NO.1034/18 Saurabh v. Rajveer & Ors. P. No. 21 of 25 ss CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2025.04.21 16:08:06 +0530 agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living.
